learning: The project is called Butterfly Platform. It is a 3D arcade gaming platform built on the Gyroid Manifold Architecture.
The core equation is z = x * y (saddle point). The Gyroid and Schwarz Diamond are the same surface via Associate Family (Bonnet rotation).
manifold-core.js is located at app/src/platform/manifold-core.js. It is the browser-side manifold substrate.
The AI engine (ManifoldAI class) is at ai/manifold-ai.js. The AI server runs on port 3377 at ai/server.js.

Groq is the primary AI provider (llama-3.3-70b-versatile). Ollama on VPS (qwen2.5-coder:1.5b) is the fallback.
Games: BrickBreaker3D, FastTrack, ZenXY (calculator/particles/synth), Manifold3D (marching cubes). All under app/src/platform/games/.
Two-labyrinth architecture: Labyrinth A = encode/write, Labyrinth B = decode/read. They never conflict. The surface between them IS the manifold.
Forbidden patterns: iterate dimensions (infinite), flatten to JSON, treat substrate as codec, straight-line shortcuts, treat encode=decode.
The owner is Ken Bingham (ken.bingham64@gmail.com, GitHub: kenbin64). The repo is butterfly-platform.
Three.js is used for 3D rendering in the browser. RAPIER is used for the physics engine.
Core substrate files: core/substrate/base-substrate.js, core/manifold/manifold.js, core/facade/manifold-facade.js, core/geometry/saddle.js.
Diamond Skeleton compression extracts only function signatures, class shapes, and exports from files — minimum material, maximum structural info.
Delta caching uses FNV-1a hashing. If conversation context unchanged, cached prompt is returned with only user message swapped. O(1) encode.
Geodesic token budgeting: system DNA 30%, user query 25%, file context 25%, memory 10%, history 10%. Total budget is provider-dependent.
The FastTrack game uses procedural track generation
